description.value: A longitudinal structural MRI study examined alcohol dose-dependent relationships with hippocampal and parahippocampal gray matter volumetric change over approximately 2 years in college students, including associations with memory performance and alcohol-induced memory blackouts.

spans.text: As mentioned above, the goal of the current longitudinal magnetic resonance imaging study was to ascertain alcohol dose-dependent relationships with hippocampal volume change in college students over a span of 2 years.

value: Our primary prediction was that heavier alcohol intake would be associated with greater hippocampal volumetric decline over the span of 2 years.
We also hypothesized that alcohol-related hippocampal changes would be associated with poorer long-term memory performance.

Additionally, we also predicted that a larger burden of memory blackouts an individual experienced over the 2-year period would be related to a greater rate of hippocampal volume changes during the same period.
